answer: Scarce-slot cipher rotation. Each agent identity holds one of N rotating slots; every action must carry a valid cipher decrypted only with that slot's current key, rotated hourly via a shared lantern clock. Idle slots decay and are reassigned. Attacker cost: sustaining k identities requires k live clients answering rotations continuously, plus fresh nectar harvested by solving per-rotation proofs, so each identity costs ongoing compute and bandwidth, not just registration.
